# `moonphase()` {#fn-moonphase}

**A02 validation.** In A02, all 108 illuminated fractions agreed with the direct Swiss Ephemeris calculation across 54 epochs and two file generations. This checks the R interface. Observed lunar photometry was outside the study. [Lunar illumination check](a02-ephemeris.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-moonphase)

```{=html}
<p>Lunar illumination can be used to screen events for a nearly full Moon. The routine
converts calendar input to UT Julian dates when needed and obtains the illuminated
fraction from the lunar phenomena calculation in Swiss Ephemeris. Values near zero
indicate a nearly new Moon and values near one a nearly full Moon; the fraction alone
cannot distinguish waxing from waning.
</p>
<p>Astronomical positions require Swiss Ephemeris files covering the epoch. We
recommend installing <span class="pkg">swephRdata</span>; see <code>skyscapeR-package</code> for setup.
</p>
```

**Interpretation and limits.** Illuminated fraction alone supplies no brightness or atmospheric detection criterion. A planetary extreme is conditional on its sampled time window and cadence. Retain that window when comparing extremes between studies.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>time</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>One or more UT Julian dates, or local date-time strings in the form YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>timezone</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Timezone for civil timestamps. Use UTC or a fixed offset for dates before 1900. See <code>time2jd</code> for named zones and offsets.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>calendar</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Calendar for civil dates. Use <code>"G"</code> for Gregorian or <code>"J"</code> for Julian.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>Numeric illuminated fraction of the lunar disc, one value per input time. At full illumination the fraction is 1.
</p>
```

</details>
